Garlic-Scallion Chicken Skewers

Skewers are the grill's oldest form on the peninsula — the jeok that sat at the center of the ceremonial table — and this record is the tabletop's weeknight version of that idea: chicken thigh cubes and scallion segments on…

Korean · Easy · Serves 4 (makes 12 skewers)

Chapter 01 / 20 meat recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: restaurant. Skewers are the grill's oldest form on the peninsula — the jeok that sat at the center of the ceremonial table — and this record is the tabletop's weeknight version of that idea: chicken thigh cubes and scallion segments on a stick, in a garlic-soy-sesame marinade light enough that the scallion survives the fire. The skewer is not decoration here; alternating meat and scallion means every bite carries the allium's sweetness against the chicken fat.

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • Thread tight but not compressed: chicken cube, scallion segment, chicken, scallion, chicken — five pieces to a skewer, the scallion segments nestled flat between the cubes so the fat shields them from direct flame. Compressed cubes cook unevenly; a finger's kiss of contact is enough.
  • Marinate 1–3 hours, skewered or loose. Chicken cubes take flavor fast; past three hours the soy's salt starts winning.
  • Reserve two tablespoons of marinade before the chicken goes in — the brush sauce is built from the clean portion, never the used bowl.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    Medium-hot fire, skewers laid across with a finger's width between them. First side undisturbed 3 minutes — the cubes need to release, and the scallion wants one face charred softly. Checkpoint — turn a test skewer: the chicken's underside should be browned with grill lines and release cleanly; the scallion's face should be charred at the tips and glossy in the middle. If the scallion is incinerated, the fire is a notch hot for its tolerance — slide the scallion ends toward the fire's cooler edge on the next round.
  2. 02
    Turn every 2 minutes through three more faces, brushing with the sauce on the second turn — 8–10 minutes total. The corners of the cubes will take little char-kisses; the centers stay juicy. Checkpoint — pull when a test cube's cut face is opaque to the center with clear juices — no pink, chicken's absolute rule — and the scallion has gone sweet-soft with char at the edges.
  3. 03
    Off the skewer at the table or straight off the stick; sesame over; cho-gochujang (#SA03) as the dip. Checkpoint — eating test: chicken and scallion from the same bite, garlic-soy glaze behind them, then the dip's sweet-heat on the finish. The stick is the portion — two skewers and rice is the honest serving. Chef’s Note — the jeok lineage deserves one honest sentence at the table: skewered meat is the grill's oldest documented form in the Korean record — the ceremonial table put a skewer at its center long before any household book wrote a bulgogi. Nothing about a weeknight chicken skewer claims that throne; it just sits, cheerfully, at the same fire's far end of history.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Scallions burnt to stringsFire too hot for themSlide toward the cooler edge; turn sooner
Cubes dryOvercooked on a clockTurn by face-browning, pull at clear juice
Skewers charred throughBamboo unsoaked30-minute soak, or metal
Bland bitesCubes too big for the window3 cm max; the full 1–3 hours

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Skewers marinate 24 hours maximum, threads and all. Cooked, 3 days — pull the meat off for a rice bowl or a wrap; the stick has done its work.
  • Variations: thread mushrooms between the cubes for the half-vegetarian table; the gochujang marinade fork (#M17's paste on cubes); beef sirloin cubes take the same build and grill a minute faster.
